arms: baseline (queried field 'tier' in the LAST column, far from the id anchor)
salient_first (queried field 'tier' moved to column 2, adjacent to the id anchor)
note: In a GCF generic tabular array the field order is declared once in the header and every row is positional, so reading a value means mapping a column position back to the header. Hypothesis: a weak model counts positions less reliably the farther the queried column sits from the id anchor (column 1), so relocating a frequently-queried column adjacent to the anchor should lift retrieval at zero token cost (same bytes, permuted header + rows). A/B moves one field ('tier') from column 12 to column 2, holding all else constant. Ran at N=60/8-col first (near ceiling, no headroom), then N=200/12-col to widen the distance. Both forms are byte-identical (21573 bytes).
finding: NEGATIVE / no-op. At N=200/12-col the relocated field 'tier' scored 3/3 on EVERY model in EVERY format — moving it from column 12 to column 2 produced zero lift. The only sub-100 cell was llama-3.1-8b dropping one question under salient_first, and that was the 'score' distance control (far in both orders), with baseline answering it correctly; single-question noise, if anything weak evidence against reordering. Models resolve a positional cell by its header-declared position regardless of distance from the anchor, because column position is pure local positional structure with no indirection. Consistent with the through-line (local structure safe, reference indirection not). This is a favorable result for the format: the tabular grammar is robust to column order, so the encoder should NOT reorder columns — doing so would only complicate multi-turn pack_root/delta stability for no comprehension gain. Not adopted into EncodeAuto.

results.note: salient_first miss was on the 'score' distance control (far in both orders), not the relocated field; baseline answered it correctly.
